mirroredFrom.rule: THIS IS A VERBATIM COPY. Edit the ledger on claude/cluster-lookahead and re-copy the whole tools/learnloop/ directory here; never the other way round. A divergence is resolved by re-copying, not by merging — one of the two is the record and the other is a convenience.

divergence.appliedHere: the 20260827-overnight fold (batch 1), applied on sim/worker-kit first
divergence.why: The local sim session fetches sim/worker-kit and only sim/worker-kit, and the updated ledger IS its next set of instructions. Waiting for a home-branch edit to be mirrored forward would have left the consumer reading a ledger that predates the batch it just ran.
divergence.scope: promotion-ledger.json and PROMOTION-STATUS.md ONLY. Nothing under lib/ or bin/ was touched, so the two copies remain byte-identical as CODE and the executable behaviour of the two branches has not forked.
divergence.backportOwed: copy tools/learnloop/promotion-ledger.json and tools/learnloop/PROMOTION-STATUS.md from sim/worker-kit onto claude/cluster-lookahead, then restore the normal direction (home edits, kit mirrors). Until that copy is made, claude/cluster-lookahead holds the STALE ledger and this branch holds the record — the reverse of the standing rule.

readMe: ONE ARTIFACT, TWO CONSUMERS. The cloud coordinator reads this to know what has
been settled; the local sim session reads it to know what to run next.
`bin/make-promotion-batch.js` turns it into the next batch's spec files, so
'what should the PC run next?' is a command and not a judgement call.
THE ONE RULE THIS LEDGER EXISTS TO ENFORCE: a deterministic probe is NECESSARY
AND NEVER SUFFICIENT. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED passed its deterministic ship gate
outright (fatal stagings 41 -> 0) and then lost snake6 1.00 -> 0.15 live, through
exhaustion — a travel-economy channel the probe does not measure. Only a live
paired sweep, with a concurrent verified null and a VERIFIED ENGAGED treatment
arm, may write a live status.

statusLadder: dark -> probe-passed  : a deterministic probe cleared its gate. Goes no further.
probe-passed -> live-* : only a live paired sweep with a verified concurrent null.
supported -> promoted  : the default flip was actually made; `promotedBy` names the commit.
frozen                 : re-opened by a MECHANISM CLAIM only, never by a p-value.
explorationSliceRule: A promoted or supported flag keeps ~10% of its cells running the OPPOSITE branch,
forever. Today's policy selects tomorrow's corpus, so a cell that turned a flag on
will otherwise never generate the data by which it could be turned back off.
powerArithmetic: A block is one seed through every cyclic seat rotation (3 games on a 3-team board).
Placement: 80% power at MDE 0.25 needs ~58 blocks on the pooled stratum, 8 on the
tightest (mix23 alone); MDE 0.10 needs 362-1,447. That is 360-1,000+ games per cell
PER ARM. Mechanism metrics move at n~8 blocks and are 5-25x outside the null band.
So: refit on mechanism, describe placement, and refuse a placement verdict from a
cell whose blocksHad < blocksNeeded. (A3 memo section 4.1.)
retiredCounters: plansEvaluated and boundsInversions are RETIRED as verdict-bearing metrics on any
live arm: at any budget they are dominated by how much CPU the process got. They
carry a verdict ONLY under a fixed-tick StepClock A/A, where the arms consume
identical work by construction. They are still reported, because they diagnose a
armEngagementRule: A live measurement must carry armEngagementVerified. `false` records the row and
moves nothing: a null from an arm that never ran is a different finding from a null
from an arm that ran and did not help. P5 is the standing exhibit — CENTAUR_WASM is
refused per partition, silently, whenever an input is not resident in linear memory.
CL7's mechanism report (TeamTurnResult.mechanism) is what makes the answer readable.
flagOrderIsPriority: THE FLAG ORDER IN THIS ARRAY IS THE BATCH ORDER. make-promotion-batch.js emits one experiment
per undecided flag in array order, and the batch is designed to be cut from the bottom when the
night is short. So reordering this array is how a priority is expressed, and it is the only
way the generator can hear one.
BATCH-1 CHANGE: CENTAUR_WASM was moved from eighth to first among the undecided flags, ahead of
CENTAUR_EDGE_EV. P5R is the only scheduled experiment in batch 2 that CLOSES a standing anomaly
rather than opening a new question, the instrumentation that makes it readable landed in CL7,
and it carries a gate that makes a broken arm impossible to misreport as a null.

ingest.result: `ingest: no arms found` — the tool refused, correctly.
ingest.why: bin/ingest.js reads <batch>/arms/<arm>/<sweepId>/manifest.jsonl. This delivery ships analysis markdown, verify-null.txt, budget-probe-v2.txt, trail-and-deaths-analysis.json and a SLIMMED manifest-core.json. There are no per-game rows anywhere in it, and per-game rows are what every number the ingest computes is computed from. There is no partial mode that helps: the null check, the pairing gate, the block CIs, the hygiene table and the engagement counters all read the same rows.
ingest.machineryVerified: The tool itself was exercised on this worktree and is sound: selftest 55/55, and the synthetic mini-batch recovers all three planted effects (the placement effect outside the noise moved CENTAUR_WASM probe-passed -> live-failed; the one inside it did not; the engagement and cap-rate plants read back). The deferral is the data, not the instrument.
ingest.deferredUntil: the 77,388,008-byte replay archive (2,592 replays, manifest.json byte-exact original) is uploaded, or the arms/ tree with manifest.jsonl is pushed to sim-results/local-20260827.
deferredRows: per-cell block CIs recomputed from rows — every effect below is transcribed from the committed analysis files, not recomputed. The analysis files and the ledger therefore share a single point of failure.
the null-band table for EVERY metric (D.nullBand over E.METRIC_KEYS). verify-null.txt gives score/win/turns on two cells; the ingest would give all 30 metrics on every cell.

the instrument-hygiene table (per-arm cap / overrun / unstaged / illegal / errors per cell) and therefore every automatic instrument EVENT: null-excludes-zero, null-band-widened, flip-rate-rose, cap-rate-asymmetry, overrun, integrity. The P5 cap-rate asymmetry is exactly the shape `cap-rate-asymmetry` exists to raise, and it was raised by a human here.

the pairing integrity gate — configHash and seat-assignment equality game by game. The batch reports 0 illegal and 0 errors over 1,824 games, but that is the harness checking itself, not the ingest checking the harness.
CENTAUR_EDGE_EV's primary metric (uncontested meals staged by contest class) — needs the replays regardless; see open item EDGE-EV-EATS.
the P7R root-cause mining pass over the seed's exhaustion deaths, which is the thing blocking P7R from being scheduled at all.

nullBandCoverage.consequence: Two of eight cells carry a measured A/A floor. Rows on the other six are read against the generic "+/-0.10 at 16 blocks" placement-resolution rule, which is a convention and not a measurement. By the ledger's own rule those rows are UNREADABLE rather than null — an absent instrument is not a finding — and that is how they are recorded below. It lands hardest on P3, whose one WIN is on snake5-queen.

flagValueAudit.question: Commit 38e15e7 warns that every CL flag parses only `1|on|true` with no warning on a typo. The batch's envAtRun stamps read "1" for the CL flags but "on" for CENTAUR_WASM and CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY and "full" for CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH. Did any arm silently run its own baseline?
flagValueAudit.answer: NO. Checked value by value against each flag's own `parses` field in this ledger. CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY parses `1|on|true`, so "on" is in its set. CENTAUR_WASM parses `on|off`, so "on" is its ONLY on-value. CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH parses `off|expiry|full`, so "full" is correct. The `1|on|true` warning applies to the five search-side CL flags, all of which were set to "1". Sixteen arms audited, zero mistyped.
flagValueAudit.arms: cl-seed{CLUSTER_SEED:1} cl-fatality{UNIT_FATALITY:1} cl-both{both:1} legacy{ENGINE:legacy} cohort-on{COHORT_POLICY:on} tier-full{TIER_TRUTH:full} wasm-on{WASM:on}; cl-off/cohort-off/tier-expiry/wasm-off/integrated/perf-substrate/slider/nullA/nullB all {}.
flagValueAudit.residualRisk: This is an audit of the ENVIRONMENT, not of what resolved inside the engine. The resolved flag stamp that would close it (MechanismReport.flags) postdates these bundles. See ENV-SEAM.

measurements.cell: cluster-seed.test.ts seedRun (26 replay positions, 40 confronted boards)
measurements.value: fatal stagings 41 -> 0; teammate kills 25 -> 4; rung-0 floor better on 18/26, mean +43.07; two -Infinity emissions rescued; emissions 57 -> 32
measurements.caveat: Final floors WORSE on 14/26 by 0.008-0.228 on floors of scale 20-100 (mean -0.05). CL1 section 6.3 named this as the open number and shipped the flag OFF because of it.

measurements.value: snake6 win rate 1.00 -> 0.15 (delta -0.854, excludes zero)
measurements.note: The effect is an order of magnitude outside the cell's own null band, so power is not the question here.
measurements.caveat: analysis-p7.md prints its standing warning on this cell: more than half of these games hit the turn cap (cl-off cap rate 0.938, cl-fatality 0.917), and the file says to treat its placement rows as UNINTERPRETABLE and raise the cap before rerunning. The cl-seed and cl-both arms escape the warning only because they die early (cap rate 0.458). The verdict survives the caveat on two independent grounds — the effect is 13-18x the cell's own measured floor, and the exhaustion mechanism is a non-placement measurement that does not route through the cap at all — but the row does not get to inherit "score -0.594" unqualified.

measurements.value: snake exhaustion deaths x1.9 (39 -> 75 over 48 games)
measurements.note: THE MECHANISM. The pairwise seed appears to disrupt snake parallel-motion and food economics — travel economy, not staging safety. The deterministic gate measures positions; this is the shape of a whole game.

measurements.value: seed+fatality together: same collapse as seed alone
measurements.note: So the cost is the seed's, not the pair's. UNIT_FATALITY alone carried no placement cost.

measurements.value: +5.1042 [+0.4423, +9.7661] over 16 blocks (excludes zero)
measurements.note: THE PIECE-DENSITY GRADIENT, first row. On the full piece roster the seed does not merely fail to hurt — it measurably helps on material. findings.md section 2 summarises the piece cells as "all three treatments null", which is true of PLACEMENT only.
measurements.ruleRefusal: CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED: a supporting cell does not overturn a live FAILURE on its own. Status stays live-failed; the failure needs a root cause and a repaired arm, not a second opinion.

measurements.value: +0.1458 [+0.0013, +0.2904] over 16 blocks (excludes zero, narrowly)
measurements.note: Second support row on the same cell and the same direction. Two ✱ rows favouring the seed where a full piece roster is present, against a catastrophic loss where none is.
measurements.ruleRefusal: CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED: a supporting cell does not overturn a live FAILURE on its own. Status stays live-failed; the failure needs a root cause and a repaired arm, not a second opinion.

measurements.value: exhaustion deaths 23 -> 48 over 48 games (x2.09)
measurements.note: THE GRADIENT`S OTHER END, and it corrects the headline. The bridge summaries carry "exhaustion x1.9", which is the null-snake6 figure (39 -> 75). snake5-knight is x2.09 — a LARGER ratio, on a cell whose placement is null. So exhaustion inflation is not a proxy for the placement collapse: it appears without one. Ordered by piece density the ratios are x2.09 (snake5-knight) / x1.92 (null-snake6) / x1.19 (headline-mix-king), and only the snake-heavy cells convert it into a loss.

UNREADABLE, not null. snake5-knight carried no A/A floor in this batch (see the batch's nullBandCoverage), so this delta has nothing to be read against. Recorded at the ledger's own standard: an absent instrument is not a finding.
measurements.ruleRefusal: CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED: live measurement recorded WITHOUT a verified null — status untouched. A treatment delta read against no null is unreadable at any size.

measurements.value: seed+fatality together: 72 exhaustion deaths over 48 games, against 75 seed-alone and 39 off
measurements.note: The joint arm reproduces the seed's exhaustion inflation almost exactly. Removing 3 of the seed's 36 extra deaths is inside the noise of a 48-game count, so the cost in this pair is the seed's and the classifier does not offset it.

flags.verdict: DO NOT PROMOTE AS-IS — and the failure is SNAKE-DENSITY-DEPENDENT, not global. The deterministic gate passed and the live arm collapsed through a channel the gate does not measure. But the collapse is confined to the cells with few or no pieces: on null-snake6 the seed loses 1.00 -> 0.15, while on headline-mix-king placement is flat and two mechanism rows (finalMaterial +5.10 ✱, survived +0.146 ✱) run in its FAVOUR. Exhaustion inflation is present everywhere the snakes outnumber the pieces (x2.09 knight, x1.92 snake6, x1.19 mix-king) but only converts into a placement loss where there is no piece play to absorb it. The live reading is therefore not "the seed is a dead idea" but "the seed is admissible on some boards and ruinous on others, and nothing currently decides which board it is on". That points at a CONDITIONAL ADMISSION future — the same shape CENTAUR_STAGING_SAFETY already ships as `auto` after helping on piece boards and regressing on snake-only — and NOT at a retirement. The status stays live-failed and the ledger's own rule is why: a failure is undone by a root cause and a repaired arm, never by other cells declining to reproduce it. The piece-cell rows are the beginning of a root cause, not a second opinion.

nextExperiment.question: Two questions now, and the second is new. (1) Is the exhaustion cost the pairwise seed itself, or the greedy basin it converges to? Two named falsifiers exist and neither needs new code: raise `restarts`, and turn `rungZeroRepair` on. (2) Is the seed CONDITIONALLY admissible — does the piece-density gradient hold up, and can the same own-board predicate that gates CENTAUR_STAGING_SAFETY's `auto` mode gate this one?
nextExperiment.blockedOn: the root-cause miner on the delivered 20260827 replays, which may answer it without new games — AND the miner cannot start until the replay archive is uploaded. That upload is now this experiment's critical path: it is the only not-scheduled item in batch 2 and the only thing standing between the program and the seed's root cause.

supportCells.headline-mix-king: SUPPORT CELL. finalMaterial +5.10 ✱ and survived +0.146 ✱ favour the seed here with placement flat. A root cause must explain why the SAME mechanism helps here and ruins null-snake6, or it is not a root cause.
supportCells.snake5-knight: THE DISCRIMINATOR, and it is new to P7R. Largest exhaustion ratio in the batch (x2.09) with NULL placement. It separates "exhaustion inflation" from "placement collapse", which the two-cell design could not: if the miner's root cause predicts a loss here, it is wrong.
supportCells.null-snake6: THE FAILING CELL. Carries the batch's cap-rate warning (cl-off 0.938); raise the cap or shorten the board before rerunning, or its placement rows arrive uninterpretable again.

nextExperiment.designNote: Batch 1 changed this experiment's shape. It was a two-cell falsifier hunt; it is now a three-cell DENSITY LADDER with a support cell at one end and the failing cell at the other, because the batch showed the effect has a sign that depends on the board. Adding snake5-knight costs one cell and is what makes the ladder a ladder.

measurements.value: measured jointly with the seed; the classifier is the weaker, set-level policy of the two
no placement cost from UNIT_FATALITY alone
measurements.note: 16 blocks against the pooled stratum's 58 for MDE 0.25. 'No placement cost' means 'no cost this cell could resolve'. That is the honest reading and it is enough to keep the flag alive; it is not enough to promote it.

measurements.value: exhaustion deaths 39 -> 33 over 48 games (x0.85) — they FALL
measurements.note: The classifier does not merely avoid the seed's failure mode, it moves slightly the other way on the very cell the seed destroyed. Absent from every bridge summary, and it is the strongest half of "fatality alone is safe". Recorded as null and not as support: 39 -> 33 over 48 games has no measured floor of its own, and one directional mechanism row does not promote anything. POLARITY WARNING: had bin/ingest.js scored this row it would have called it FAILED, because its verdict rule reads any negative mechanism delta as a failure and it does not know that fewer deaths is better. See open item METRIC-POLARITY.

measurements.value: seed+fatality together: 72 deaths over 48 games, against 75 for the seed alone and 39 off
measurements.note: THE BOUNDARY OF THE CLASSIFIER`S CLAIM, and deliberately not a failure verdict. Written as `failed` in the first pass of this fold, it moved UNIT_FATALITY live-null -> live-failed — and that was a mis-attribution the rules made visible: the 72 deaths are the SEED's cost, recorded against CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED where they belong. All this row says about the classifier is what it does NOT do: it is safe alone, and it is not a repair for something else.

flags.verdict: Alive, unpromoted, and cheaper than it looked. It costs nothing measurable in placement (16 blocks against the pooled stratum's 58, so "no cost this cell could resolve"), it demonstrably runs, and on null-snake6 exhaustion deaths FALL under it (39 -> 33). What it has still never been shown to do is buy anything on its own. Note the asymmetry the batch settled: the cl-both arm reproduces the seed's collapse almost exactly (-0.573 vs -0.594; 72 deaths vs 75), so the cost in that pair is the seed's and not the pair's — but equally, the classifier is not a repair for the seed.

nextExperiment.question: Does the classifier buy fatal-staging reduction on PIECE boards when the seed is off — i.e. is it promotable independently of the flag that failed?

promotionMetrics.name: wasmRuns
promotionMetrics.note: THE GAP THAT VOIDED P5. Existed on the territory workspace since W3 and was unreachable outside evaluate/territory.ts.

measurements.value: placement NULL
measurements.note: STATUS UNMOVED BY THIS ROW. Engagement was unverifiable at the time — wasmRuns did not leave the module — so a null here could equally mean the arm never engaged.
measurements.caveat: ENGAGEMENT VOCABULARY. `armEngagementVerified: false` is carried on this row because false is the only value the current applyMeasurement refuses on. The honest value is `null` — CANNOT SAY. wasmRuns was never read and returned zero here; it did not exist in these bundles at all. The ledger's stated tri-state (null = cannot say, false = read and was zero) and its enforcement disagree, and this row is where the disagreement is being papered over. Left as false deliberately: correcting it to null on this branch would UNBLOCK a status write that must stay blocked, and the one-line fix belongs on the home branch. See ENGAGEMENT-TRISTATE.

rootCauseKnown.diagnosis: kit commit 38e15e7: the wasm arm "is refused per partition, silently, and its counters never left the module they lived in". CL7`s telemetry closure fixed both halves — tapWitnesses was dropping the accessors, and release() was erasing the session-derived reports before any external consumer could read them — and manifest rows now carry wasmRuns / wasmRefused.
rootCauseKnown.doesNotUpgradeThisRow: THE FIX IS PRE-HOC FOR THE PROGRAM AND POST-HOC FOR THIS BATCH. Batch 1`s bundles were built from 8059b86, which predates the counters. A diagnosis that arrived after the games were played does not make the games readable. P5 stays engagement-unverified FOR THIS BATCH, and the presence of the fix is a reason to re-run, not a reason to re-score.

measurements.value: cap-terminal rate DOUBLES under wasm-on on headline-mix-king: 0.229 -> 0.458 (x2.0); and goes 0.917 -> 1.000 on null-snake6, where it saturates
measurements.note: A doubled cap rate with null placement is a real shape change. Suspects, in the order the record ranks them: (1) the env-vs-options seam across workers — the flag is per-engine and the pool may not carry it; (2) the WSL wasm build/load path; (3) the arm is genuinely slower there. The engagement counters separate (1) and (2) from (3) in one run.
measurements.caveat: THE ANOMALY IS A CLUSTER OF FOUR ROWS, NOT ONE RATE. Bridge summaries carry only the doubled cap rate. On the same cell, wasm-on games also run ~21 turns LONGER (+21.44 ✱), take ~22 more decisions (+21.75 ✱) and end LESS decisively (-0.2292 ✱ — decisive 0.771 -> 0.542), and on null-snake6 the cap rate saturates at 1.000. Four independent rows pointing the same way with placement dead flat: something changes materially about how games TERMINATE while leaving the ranking untouched. Score the anomaly on the cluster; a single rate is dismissable and the cluster is not.

measurements.note: Anomaly corroborant 1. Clears the cell's own measured floor, but not by much — this is the weakest of the four rows on its own and the most convincing in company.

flags.verdict: THE ONE MEASURED ANOMALY ON THE BRANCH, AND IT IS STILL UNREADABLE. Placement is null on all three cells and that null is worth nothing: the arm cannot be shown to have run. Meanwhile four shape rows on the same cell say the games changed — twice the cap rate, ~21 more turns, ~22 more decisions, a quarter less decisive — and shape rows never move a status by rule, which is correct and is also exactly why this flag cannot be resolved from batch 1 at all. The root cause is already named upstream (refused per partition, silently; counters trapped in the module) and CL7 closed the telemetry, so the decisive experiment is now cheap and unambiguous. P5R IS THAT EXPERIMENT and it is the highest-value run in batch 2: it is the only scheduled experiment that resolves a standing anomaly rather than opening a new question, and its gate makes it impossible to mis-report — wasmRuns 0 on the treatment arm is a BROKEN ARM and must be reported as a refusal, not as a null.

nextExperiment.question: With engagement on the record: did the wasm arm run at all, and is the doubled cap rate a slower arm or a refused one?
nextExperiment.gate: REFUSE THE CELL if wasmRuns is 0 on the treatment arm. That is not a null, it is a broken arm, and reporting it as a null is exactly the error this rerun exists to correct.
nextExperiment.requires: A bundle built from a tip at or after the CL7 telemetry closure, so TeamTurnResult.mechanism exists.
nextExperiment.priority: HIGHEST of the probe-passed flags, and raised by batch 1. CENTAUR_WASM has been moved ahead of the never-raced flags in this ledger's flag order, which is the order the batch generator emits and therefore the order the batch is cut from the bottom in. Reason: every other scheduled experiment opens a question, and this one closes the batch's only measured anomaly with instrumentation that now exists. If the night is short, P5R survives the cut.
nextExperiment.decisiveBecause: The four-row shape cluster has exactly three candidate explanations and one run separates them. wasmRuns == 0 on the treatment arm: the arm never engaged, the cap-rate cluster is something else entirely, and the P5 null was never about wasm. wasmRuns > 0 with wasmRefused high: the per-partition refusal is real and the arm is paying a check it never cashes. wasmRuns > 0 with wasmRefused low and the cluster still present: the arm genuinely runs and genuinely changes how games terminate, which is a finding worth the whole batch.
nextExperiment.addedReadsOut: the batch-1 anomaly cluster must be read out in full, not just capRate: turns, decisions and decisive, or the rerun cannot confirm or clear the thing it exists to resolve.

openInstrumentItems.what: bin/ingest.js decides a verdict by SIGN ALONE: a mechanism or placement delta outside the null band scores `failed` if its mean is negative and `supports-promotion` if positive. It has no notion of which metrics are better when they go DOWN. So deathsExhaustion, deathsSelf, fatalStagings, teammateKills, place, boundsInversions, overrunRate and every other cost-shaped counter are scored exactly backwards.
openInstrumentItems.impact: SEVERE, AND THE EXHIBIT IS THIS LEDGER`S FOUNDING FINDING. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED's failure is an exhaustion-death INCREASE of +36 per 48 games on a metric declared family:mechanism. Run through the ingest, that positive delta scores `supports-promotion`. It is caught here only because the flag is ALREADY live-failed and "a supporting cell does not overturn a live failure" refuses it — i.e. the ledger is saved by a different rule, and would not have been had the flag still been probe-passed when the row arrived. Two further rows in the batch-1 fold trip it in the other direction: UNIT_FATALITY's exhaustion deaths FALLING 39 -> 33 would score `failed`, and TERRITORY_SLIDER_PROFILE's place improving by -0.229 would score `failed`. All three are recorded by hand with the correct verdict and a polarity note.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: The fold declares `lowerIsBetter: true` on the affected promotionMetrics entries of CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED and CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY. Nothing reads the field yet. It exists so the fix is a lookup rather than a re-derivation.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: A one-line change on claude/cluster-lookahead, in bin/ingest.js's verdict expression: consult the gate's `lowerIsBetter` and flip the sign test. Plus the polarity declarations on the remaining gate metrics, and a selftest assertion that a falling death count does not read as a failure. NOT applied here: this branch is the mirror and its code must not fork from home.

openInstrumentItems.what: The ledger documents `armEngagementVerified` as a tri-state — true = shown engaged, false = a counter was READ and was zero, null = CANNOT SAY (an old bundle) — and README.md states the rule as "a live measurement on an arm whose engagement is not SHOWN moves nothing". applyMeasurement refuses only on `=== false`. `null` sails through and may write a live status.
openInstrumentItems.impact: Every batch predating the CL7 mechanism report has null engagement on every row, which is the common case and not the edge case. The seeded ledger hides the gap by marking CENTAUR_WASM's batch-1 rows `false` — a value the vocabulary reserves for a counter that was read — because false is the only value that actually refuses. The datum was bent to fit the code. The fold leaves it bent ON PURPOSE and says so on the row, because correcting it to the honest `null` on this branch would unblock a status write that must stay blocked.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: CENTAUR_WASM's rows keep `false` with a caveat naming this item. CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH's row, which is NOT load-bearing for a refusal, is corrected to the honest `null` and carries an engagementEvidence block.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: On claude/cluster-lookahead: change `if (m.armEngagementVerified === false)` to refuse on anything that is not `true`, add the selftest assertion for the null case, then correct CENTAUR_WASM's two batch-1 rows to `null` in the same commit. All three selftest engagement cases pass explicit booleans, so the tightening is assertion-safe.

openInstrumentItems.what: bin/make-promotion-batch.js hard-codes the A/A null's cells as headline-mix-king and null-snake6, regardless of which cells the batch's treatments actually run on. Batch 1 therefore measured a floor for two of its eight cells, and batch 2 as generated repeats the pattern: P5R runs hazard-mix-king, P3`s support cells are snake5-queen and snake5-knight, and none of them will get a floor.
openInstrumentItems.impact: By the ledger's own rule, a metric with no floor in the A/A cell is UNREADABLE and not null, so an uncovered cell cannot produce a verdict at all — it produces a row that must be recorded and refused. Batch 1 spent six of eight cells this way. It also lands on the ledger's single best result: TERRITORY_SLIDER_PROFILE's only win is on snake5-queen and clears a BORROWED mix-king floor by 0.018.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: Uncovered cells are recorded with nullVerified: false and verdict `unreadable`, which is what the rules already demand. Add the missing cells to the N0 spec by hand before running batch 2.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: On claude/cluster-lookahead: derive the A/A null's cells from the union of the scheduled specs` cells instead of the hard-coded pair, so the floor is measured wherever a treatment is read. It costs box time and it is the cheapest box time in the batch — an unfloored treatment cell is games spent on a row nobody may read.

openInstrumentItems.what: applyMeasurement has no concept of a CONTROL cell. A cell that is null BY DESIGN — a provably-inert path included precisely to prove the instrument reports zero when zero is the truth — is indistinguishable to the rules from a treatment cell that failed to show an effect, and it takes the same `live-null` branch.
openInstrumentItems.impact: Demonstrated live during the batch-1 fold. TERRITORY_SLIDER_PROFILE's null-snake6 control sat at EXACTLY 0 against a measured +/-0.0324 floor — the strongest single row in the ledger, because it shows the measurement is not manufacturing effects — and filing it as family `placement` demoted the flag `supported` -> `live-null`. The better the control, the harder it demotes. This is a rule that punishes the practice it exists to encourage.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: The row is filed as family `audit`, which never moves a status and is arguably its true family anyway: an inert control is evidence about the INSTRUMENT, not a placement claim about the treatment. Recorded on the row itself so the choice is not mistaken for a dodge.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: On claude/cluster-lookahead: an explicit `control: true` on a measurement, refused from moving a status and rendered as a distinct badge; plus a selftest asserting that a passing control does not demote a supported flag. Until then `audit` is the correct filing and the note carries the reasoning.

openInstrumentItems.what: L.undecided() returns dark, probe-passed and live-failed. A `live-null` flag is treated as settled, so make-promotion-batch.js never schedules its nextExperiment — even when the ledger has written one out in full and even when the null came from a cell the ledger itself marked underpowered.
openInstrumentItems.impact: Three flags are affected and their named experiments are unreachable from the generator: CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY (P7F — "is the classifier promotable independently of the flag that failed?"), CENTAUR_TIER_TRUTH (P4R, separately blocked on P11) and CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY (P6R, separately deferred on counters). UNIT_FATALITY is the sharp case: its null is explicitly "no cost this cell could resolve" at 16 blocks against 58 needed, which is not a decision, and P7F silently never runs.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: None applied. P7F is named here so it is visible to a reader of the status page even though the generator will not emit it.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: On claude/cluster-lookahead, one of: include live-null flags whose last placement row is `underpowered` in undecided(); or add an explicit `scheduleAnyway` field to nextExperiment. The first is principled and the second is honest about being a manual override.

standingExperiments.title: The budget ladder
standingExperiments.approvedBy: owner — pre-approved, conditional on budget-probe v2 confirming
standingExperiments.trigger: CONFIRMED, and here is the whole arithmetic. budget-probe v2, 60 recorded positions drawn from 480 integrated replays, idle box, FRESH ENGINE PER POSITION, sample seed 1, 9 skipped: a true 1000 ms run reproduces the 2000 ms decision on 55 of 60 positions. FLIPS 5/60 = 8.3% (+/-7.0). A/A FLOOR, 2000 ms against itself: 1/60 = 1.7% (+/-3.2). EXCESS ATTRIBUTABLE TO BUDGET = 6.7 points, wide at n=60 and the intervals overlap — the direction is clear and the magnitude is not. The condition on the owner's pre-approval is met.
standingExperiments.question: Where on the budget curve does the substrate stop being speed and start being strength? P1 found the perf substrate was speed-not-strength at 2000 ms; the bimodal revision result (65% of decisions settle by 250 ms, 34.8% revise in a wave at 1000-1500 ms, nothing between) says 1000 ms would amputate the second pass entirely. Three points draw the line.
standingExperiments.designNote: ONE trail-instrumented cell in the ladder. The 35% revision wave was measured PRE-CL3, and cluster enumeration front-loads coordination, so the wave's own shape may have moved — which would make the ladder's middle rung mean something different from what it meant last month. Mechanism-first at 8 blocks: placement is descriptive here, not claimable. BATCH-1 NOTE: the 500 ms rung is now the interesting one. If the deep pass lands at 1000-1500 ms and the engine reschedules it under a 1 s budget, then 1000 ms may barely differ from 2000 ms while 500 ms amputates the pass outright — so the ladder's information is concentrated at its bottom rung.
standingExperiments.caveat: CHANGED != IMPROVED, and nothing measures the difference. The 35.0%/60.1% figures count decisions whose staged move-set changed; the 8.3% counts decisions a shorter budget decides differently. Whether those ~7% are BETTER is unmeasured and is exactly what the ladder is for.
standingExperiments.reconciliation: TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY DISAGREE, AND DO NOT. The emission trails say 35.0% (P4, 50,455 decisions) and 60.1% (P5, 52,191) of decisions differ from what was staged at 1000 ms. budget-probe v2 says a true 1 s budget reproduces the 2 s decision 91.7% of the time. Both are right. The last-emission histogram shows the engine stages an incumbent in under 250 ms in 99.9% of decisions and then either never revises or revises in a single wave landing at 1000-1500 ms — the 250-1000 ms window is EMPTY, 8 decisions out of 102,646. The engine is deadline-aware: under a 1 s budget it RESCHEDULES the deep pass rather than losing it. So "what was on the table at 1000 ms" and "what a 1000 ms engine decides" are different questions, and only the second is the one the ladder asks. Net: the second second changes about 7% of decisions.
standingExperiments.retracted: budget-probe v1 IS RETRACTED — DO NOT INGEST. It reused one engine across games, and engines carry per-game ledger state, so its results were degenerate (0/60 flips in 26 s). Fixed in 65aa973. If a v1 file turns up in the archive, it is not evidence.
